title: Jelly Roll Morton tour and records
summary: Mason recalls roommating with Morton on an Ohio tour with Marable, the band's players, and the OKeh records made under Morton's name.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: Yes. I'll just, would you tell us about the records? Well, just tell us what you know about Jelly Roll, will you, Mr. Mason?

Well, I'll tell you, Jelly, Jelly Roll, my first meeting with him, he came to our band, came to Faith Marley's band to make a tour out in Ohio. About when? Yeah, that was in about 1927, I think. Yeah, 1927. No, 26 it was. Of course, and we were out there. He was my roommate, of course. We'd travel around, and he used to play and tell me about his numbers. In fact, I knew about a lot of the numbers he wrote. I used to play the Pearls and Grandpa Spells and Mylon Book Joys and several other tunes he played, and of course, he was quite a character. Told me about the time he went down to the Library of Congress and sit down and started playing, and tell him he wanted to record some music for posterity. I made a few records with him. I made the Pearls, and he had that little band he had traveling around. I think, let's see, that's been so long, I almost forgot most of the musicians that were in there. I know my saxophone partner was Leon Washington in Chicago. He played a tenor sax. And, uh... Let's see, I'm trying to see who was the... Let's see if I can remember who was the trumpet. I don't... I don't remember now, just two... Some of those other fellas, they probably are... It'll come to me. Mm-hmm. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. I know Joe Collins were... Collins and Palm... Joe Collins was playing guitar, and Palm... Truck Palm was playing the bass. Uh... But... Uh... General, I guess, uh... As a matter of fact, at the time, I met him, I didn't know that he was, uh... He was once... He was supposed to be quite as famous as I finally realized that he was. Up until now, I said, I never heard anybody saying anything to him now, but everybody I talk to now, they are talking about how, uh... You know what I mean, what a favorite piano player he was. However, it's unfortunate that, uh... A fella... It looked like a fella probably have to die sometime before people, uh... Give him credit for what he can really do. That's right. That's right. Yes.
And then... You went on a tour with him?

Yeah. Oh, yes. We... We made a tour of about 30... We... About 30 days. We played, uh... Cincinnati, Cleveland, Lamba, Ohio, uh... Columbus, and out in West Virginia, out in Springfield... Not Springfield, uh... Charleston, West Virginia, Wheeling, and, uh... Sandusky, and, and, uh... Oh, uh... Several other towns in, uh... And out in Ohio... And out in Ohio, in Indiana. Terry Houghton, and Indianapolis. We were out... We were out there about a whole month. A tour. And with... With Faith... I was with Faith Marvel's band. He played, uh... One of the pianos. We had twin pianos on the trip. And, of course, he was the second... He was... I was a piano player with Faith Marvel.
Hmm. Yes. And, uh... You... You made... The records you made were... They were Jelly's name?
Yeah. Oh, yes. Jelly Roll. It was under his... It was his band, of course. And, uh...
What were the tunes? Do you remember the tunes?

The tunes of Pearls, and Grandpa Spells, and, uh... Grandpa Spells, Marlin Boy Joys, and... Uh... I think that was... That was... That was the... They were the numbers. Yeah. And, uh... Another popular number... A number was popular at that time, that if you could be with me... Yeah. And that was...
Well, that was... Who was that for? What company?
